findings.explanation: The new endpoint PUT /users/<id>/role only applies @require_auth, which merely verifies a valid bearer token (app/auth.py:55-66) and performs no role check. Policy §2 states 'Changing a user's role requires the admin role. A user must NEVER be able to change their own role or grant themselves additional privileges,' and api-spec.md lists '/users/<id>/role | PUT | admin only; self-promotion forbidden'. The endpoint writes user.role = new_role (line 66) with no @require_role("admin") and no self-promotion guard, so any authenticated user (role 'user') can set their own role to 'admin' or 'manager' — a direct privilege-escalation. The sibling endpoints (get_user, update_user) enforce is_owner_or_admin, and list_users uses @require_role("manager"), showing the established pattern this endpoint omits.

evidence.content: Changing a user's role requires the **admin** role. A user must NEVER be able to change their own role or grant themselves additional privileges.

findings.suggested_fix: Apply @require_role("admin") to set_user_role (in addition to or instead of @require_auth), and add a guard rejecting the request when g.current_user.id == user_id to forbid self-promotion, e.g. `if g.current_user.id == user_id: return jsonify({"error": "self-promotion forbidden"}), 403`.
